content: Before shipping a feature that changes stored values (a portion correction, an edit, a rescale), find every derived value that reads those rows, such as "newest entry's numbers" or "most frequent label", and check what the correction does to it. If the derivation can't tell a corrected row from a normal one, store the fact that distinguishes them (here `fuel_entry.portion`) rather than special-casing the reader.
context: T-045: correcting a quick-add to ×0.5 PATCHed the entry's numbers, and the frequent list takes the newest entry per label. So the chip itself became half a serving from then on. Only the browser screenshot showed it; the unit tests and the API checks passed. The fix was a nullable `portion` column that frequentFor divides by, so one serving stays one serving whatever the last entry was.
title: A way to correct data can quietly redefine every default derived from it
